tracker_name: Texas Autonomous Fleet Tracker (Texas AV Tracker)
method_notes: Site pulls directly from the Texas DMV (TxDMV) Automated Vehicle Registry created under Texas SB 2807 (effective 2026-05-28), which legally requires AV operators to register fleet counts; site states it 'auto-updates every 60 seconds' from that registry. Count of 577 is the statewide Waymo figure as reported by TechCrunch's coverage of the same underlying registry launch, not a number WebFetch could directly render live (dashboard is JS-driven) - value taken from https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/28/waymo-dominates-texas-autonomous-vehicle-registrations-as-tesla-trails-behind/ which cites the identical registry.
confidence_notes: High confidence in the underlying registry (it is a state regulatory data source with legal reporting obligations), but WebFetch could only retrieve the tracker's static page shell (methodology text), not the live per-city numeric table, because the counts render client-side. The 577 figure is therefore sourced via a news article reading the same registry rather than a direct scrape of texasavtracker.com's live numbers on 2026-07-22. Also does not break the 577 down by individual TX city (Austin vs Dallas vs Houston vs San Antonio).

tracker_name: SF Examiner fleet disclosure (cited via thelastdriverlicenseholder.com and Driverless Digest)
method_notes: Not a crowdsourced tracker - this is investigative journalism in which the SF Examiner repeatedly pressed Waymo directly for fleet numbers over multiple months (reporting 'over 300' in March 2025, then '800+' by August 2025), and cross-referenced against CPUC filings showing 1,429 vehicles registered statewide for CA operations, 875 based at SF depots.
confidence_notes: Included here because it is the closest thing to an independent 'audit' of Waymo's own disclosures for a single geography, and is more rigorous than most crowdsourced trackers, but it is fundamentally still self-reported-to-a-journalist data, not an automated scrape.

estimated_vehicle_count: 3067 (5th-gen system, per Dec 2025 filing) / 3871 (per June 2026 recall filing covering nearly all 5th-gen vehicles)
method_notes: Federal regulatory filings Waymo is legally required to submit; recall notices (e.g. the 2026-06 freeway-construction-zone recall of 'nearly 3,900' vehicles, and a 2026-05 flooded-roads recall of ~3,800) implicitly disclose fleet-wide fifth-generation vehicle counts because they describe the number of vehicles subject to a software OTA fix.
confidence_notes: Treated as the closest thing to an 'official' fleet count Waymo has, since it is filed with a federal regulator, but WebFetch was not used to pull NHTSA's raw SGO database directly (site requires interactive querying); figures here are as reported by CNBC, Fox 5 Atlanta, and Detroit News coverage of the filings. Does not include 6th-gen (Zeekr 'Ojai' / Hyundai IONIQ 5) vehicles, which were only beginning to roll out (May 2026 onward) and would be on a separate SGO filing.
